title: Classic Olympic Physique: Phase 1
author: Mithosphere
desc:
Train 2 days on, 1 day off

Day 1: Legs and Calves - Shoulders
Day 2: Chest / Triceps
Day 3: Conditioning
Day 4: Shoulders / Biceps/ Calves
Day 5: Back
Day 6: Conditioning
Day 1: Repeat

The original standard for a classic physique was that your calves and arms should measure the same. If any single muscle rates as the least developed of all muscles among bodybuilders – it’s the calf. They are stubborn and difficult to develop and require special attention. So don’t neglect your calf work.

Don’t be in a big rush to use as much weight as possible in each exercise. Try to leave each workout knowing you can improve in at least one exercise the next time you workout.

The Hack Squat is preferred, if you have the equipment available.

A feeder workout is performed two days after your primary workout for a specific body part. Included are feeder workouts for the shoulders, lats, and calves – full development of these body parts are essential in developing a classic physique. 

Workout Notes:
Day 1:
- Shoulder Feeder Workout: Shoulder width is key to developing a classic physique, that’s why it is our first “feeder” workout.

Day 2:
- For Bench Press: Dumbbells are preferred if you can give up the barbell bench press in developing squared off “gladiator pecs” preferred in the classic physique. 
- For Dumbbell Pullovers: “The serratus magnus muscles are the ‘jewel-like’ muscles of your chest … they add width to the chest, shape, muscular definition – as well as classic beauty.” ~ Vince Gironda.
- Back Feeder Workout: Shoulder-width Parallel-grip Pulldown (for width) or Under-grip Cable Seated Rows (for back density). 

Day4:
Calf Feeder Workout: Standing Calf Raise: warm-up x 10-15 reps, 4x25, 1x100 (no weight on the 100-rep set unless you can get the full 100 reps without resting.) Remember what we said earlier about calves. You must bomb them into growth.

Day 5:
Choose One Feeder Workout, not both:
Chest: Incline Flyes - if your chest is a weak point.
Quads: Smith Machine Squats - if your quads are a weak point.

The program is broken into three separate blocks with the main lifts progressing to more technical and power-developing variants.

Lastly, on the conditioning days, we employ the Javorek Barbell Complex #1 to more fully develop the yoke and look of power, as well as adding in a certain level of conditioning that doesn't involve direct cardio. The complex uses a clean grip and is intended to performed without dropping the bar.
Perform in a non-stop, continuous order as listed:
- 6 x Barbell Upright Row
- 6 x Barbell High Pull Snatch
- 6 x Barbell Behind the Neck Squat Push Press
- 6 x Barbell Good Morning
- 6 x Barbell Bent Over Row
- 6 x Barbell High Pull Snatch
